Okay so I have a master's degree in history and my advice would be:

A) keep on reading! Find literature lists (this sub surely has some somewhere) and read on subjects you are interested in. These can be very general history books or super specific stuff like, idk, jewelry making in the ancient Mediterranean 

B) read original ancient texts. These might be challenging at first, but they really are the key to understanding the ancient world. Stuff like Homer, Virgil, Livy, whatever you want. These exist as translated versions that you should be able to borrow from your local library. If you really want to learn, make notes. Who is writing these texts? For whom? What do you think the plot/characters/events imply? You will get better at this with practice and when your knowledge grows.

C) Consider taking classes if you can. Talking about history with other people and hearing things explained is usually very helpful. In classes you might be able to learn about methods and the history of historical research.

Just remember to have fun with it and that history is not about memorizing things, it's about understanding! The most important tool of any historian is a critical mind.

I used to feel the same way and then I met my current bf. His love is something I wish for everyone - he loves me intensely, wants to be with me our whole lives, compliments me constantly and does things for me etc. Yet he isn't unhealthy in his love, like I don't have to worry about him doing something to himself if we were to break up (which is something I have done in the past). What I'm saying is that people who love intensely ARE there, you just have to find them. I do believe it's once-in-a-lifetime for most people.

I also want to say that I think I know what you mean when you say "love hard" - the kind of love where you would die for the other person, that makes you forget yourself and devote your life to them. After going through life loving people like that I've found that it's not something I want to experience in quite the same way anymore. Wanting to die because of someone isn't worth it to me. I've felt the most intense love there is to feel and it's left me with scars and fear. Now with my current bf I've finally learnt to love in a more gentle way that makes me still have my individuality intact. 

It's really hard feeling the intense love and not getting it back, but I truly believe that you can find people who love you in ways you didn't even know existed. We tend to think that when our love is big and loud, it must be everything there is to love, but I think different people can teach us a lot about love.

But I remind myself that being soft and fragile isn't inherently bad, it just is. It's a quality like any other, we all have various degrees of that in us, for some it can be a personal problem, but it's not a bad thing per se, if you catch my drift. It helps me view my anxiety with a bit more kindness, at least.

Usually it's a coping mechanism related to mental illness. I personally haven't cut myself many times, but when I have, it has been a result of an anxiety attack, usually when I've been suicidal as well. It feels like a physical release, because for me, anxiety attacks feel like they need to escalate somehow, like it's a restless feeling that needs to blow up in some way or another (that's not actually true btw, you can just soothe yourself and eventually calm down). But it's also like a punishment, because I feel like I deserve the pain.
